social.hook: He opened with 'Steppin' Out' and closed with 'I'm the Man' — twenty songs between them.
social.caption: First time seeing Joe Jackson, August 2003. I didn't get back to another of his shows until 2012.
beats: 'Steppin' Out' as the opener: he led with the thing everyone came for and still had nineteen songs left to play.
Twenty songs in a single set. By the time he closed with 'I'm the Man', nothing felt rushed.
This was 2003 — the same year I saw Peter Gabriel, The Human League and The Cure. Joe Jackson fit right in that company.
Nine years passed before I saw him again. I didn't know that night it would be that long.

social.hook: Four times in 25 years, and the opener slot barely counts.
social.caption: I saw The Smithereens four times across 25 years — but one of those was an opening set, not a headline. Birchmere in 2016 was the real fourth.
beats: The Smithereens opened for someone else in 1991. I filed it, but it didn't fully count.
Three headline sets across 25 years is a thin thread for a band this good.
Birchmere in 2016 was my only time in that room — and my most recent Smithereens show.
The opener slot from 1991 still bothers me a little. Four visits, but one of them was borrowed.

social.hook: They opened with 'Being Boiled' and closed with 'Together in Electric Dreams' — 17 songs between.
social.caption: The Human League's first of three times I'd see them, with The English Beat opening. I didn't go back for 15 years.
beats: The English Beat opened. That alone made it a strange and excellent night before The Human League played a note.
'Being Boiled' first — one of their earliest songs, cold and mechanical, as a way to say hello.
17 songs later they closed on 'Together in Electric Dreams', which is about as perfect an exit as a setlist can have.
I saw Peter Gabriel, Joe Jackson and The Cure that same year. This night still stands out for how it started and ended.
It would be 15 years before I saw them again. I didn't know that walking out.

social.hook: They closed with 'Love Will Tear Us Apart.' I didn't see them again for 37 years.
social.caption: New Order opened with 'State of the Nation' and closed with a Joy Division song — 14 songs deep into a night that took 37 years to repeat.
beats: August 23, 1985. New Order, first time — A Certain Ratio and Abecedarians opened.
They opened with 'State of the Nation' and played 14 songs before the last one.
The last one was 'Love Will Tear Us Apart.' It wasn't a New Order song. It landed anyway.
I didn't see them again until 2022. Thirty-seven years is a long time to sit with a setlist.
